items.claim: The row's seam warrant is sound: the seeing-and-naming exchange closing at 24:3 is properly bounded by the fresh, verse-initial word-event formula opening at 24:4, and both the unit_type and the parent frame assignment match the ruled architecture.
items.evidence: Jer.24.1 opens on the seeing formula and Jer.24.3 closes the naming exchange with Yahweh's question and Jeremiah's answer, both spliced byte-true to source; Jer.24.4, excluded from this row, opens with the vayehi-devar-YHWH formula at a verse-initial site, distinguishing the interpretive half that follows as a genuine tier-1 seam rather than an arbitrary or cap-driven cut. vision_report and the frame spanning Jer.21.1 to Jer.24.10 both match the ruled architecture. The setumah disclosures at Jer.23.40 and Jer.24.2 and the petuchah disclosure at Jer.24.3 all check out against the single-witness mark inventory.
tier_citations: word-event formula: verse-initial vayehi-devar-YHWH member at Jer.24.4
single-witness marks: setumah Jer.23.40, setumah Jer.24.2, petuchah Jer.24.3

items.claim: The row correctly holds the vision's good-figs and bad-figs interpretation together as one unit under a shared word-event opening, and its rejected alternative of splitting at the good/bad turn is a genuine, non-strawman rival properly set aside on the matching-construction evidence.
items.evidence: Jer.24.4 opens the interpretation on its own word-event formula; the matching comparison constructions at Jer.24.5 and Jer.24.8 are both byte-true splices sharing one grammatical shape, supporting the claim that no addressee, scene, or discourse-imperative seam separates the good-figs half from the bad-figs half, and no fresh tier-1 device opens at Jer.24.8 itself. The medium confidence and frontier flag are proportionate to the real content divergence between the two halves rather than overclaiming certainty. The ketiv/qere disclosure at Jer.24.9 and the setumah/petuchah disclosures at Jer.24.7, Jer.24.3, and Jer.24.10 all check out.
tier_citations: single-witness marks: setumah Jer.24.7, petuchah Jer.24.3, petuchah Jer.24.10

items.claim: The row's prose correctly distinguishes Jer.25.1's concerning-form header from the book's to-form el-Yirmeyahu word-event class, but its structured signal tag for that header reuses the same base label as the true eleven-verse class without any qualifier marking it as a separate, one-site count object.
items.evidence: Jer.25.1 reads “The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah” (web:Jer.25.1), and the row's own prose correctly names the underlying preposition as the concerning-form rather than the to-form carried by the book's eleven-verse prose-sermon-superscription class (7:1, 11:1, 18:1, 21:1, 30:1, 32:1, 34:1, 34:8, 35:1, 40:1, 44:1). The row's signal tag for this header, however, is an unqualified word-event label identical to the stem of the true el-class tag, rather than a label distinguishing it as its own count object. Because the word-event system is ruled as three shapes that must never blend, and this one-site header has already been mis-filed into the eleven-verse list once in this book's own editorial record, a structured tag that cannot be told apart from that class's tag is a live hazard for any downstream count of it, independent of the row's own correct prose.
tier_citations: byte tier: oshb:Jer.25.1 (concerning-form preposition, not the to-form)
word-event class inventory: eleven-verse el-Yirmeyahu list, Jer.25.1 excluded as its own count object

items.claim: The row calibrates its 25:8 seam honestly, declining to assert a frame-owner change where the divine speaker does not in fact change across it, and it holds the 25:13 self-reference open as an unresolved scope question rather than silently resolving it.
items.evidence: The neum closure at Jer.25.7 and the “Therefore Yahweh of Armies says” (web:Jer.25.8) koh-amar-tsevaot onset are both byte-confirmed, and the row explicitly discloses that the speaker does not change across that seam, correctly declining to treat a bare koh-amar onset as a frame-owner-change seam on its own. At Jer.25.13 the row discloses the self-referential scope of “all that is written in this book” (web:Jer.25.13) as unresolved by this tiling and reduces confidence accordingly, without invoking any cross-tradition material for or against a boundary there. The rejected alternative -- one fourteen-verse unit from the header through the recompense clause -- is conceded as also defensible, a genuine rather than strawman rival.
tier_citations: byte tier: oshb:Jer.25.7 (neum closure), oshb:Jer.25.8 (koh-amar tsevaot onset), oshb:Jer.25.13
single-witness marks: setumah Jer.25.7, setumah Jer.25.14

items.claim: The row correctly applies the one-unit rule to the cup complex by holding the command, the compliance report, and the enforcement clause together, discloses its unit_type as a structural analogy that falls outside the book's eight named symbolic acts rather than asserting settled membership, and leaves the cup's relationship to the later nations material open.
items.evidence: The private commission at Jer.25.15, the compliance report at Jer.25.17, and the enforcement command at Jer.25.27 are all byte-confirmed and share the same addressee -- the nations already made to drink -- supporting the row's rejection of a split at 25:27 as a real, non-strawman rival correctly set aside rather than a strawman. The device notes disclose that this unit falls outside the book's eight named symbolic acts (loincloth, potter, flask, yoke, field, Rechabites, stones, scroll), satisfying the disclosure duty for an operative-category deviation rather than silently asserting settled membership in that set. The row's closing sentence leaves open whether the cup anticipates the later nations material, matching this book's own flagged hazard at the chapter-25 pivot, and confidence is reduced accordingly.
tier_citations: single-witness marks: setumah Jer.25.14, setumah Jer.25.27

items.claim: The row correctly declines to treat the koh-amar-tsevaot onset at 25:32 as a row seam because it carries no change of speaker from the neum-closed line immediately before it, correctly applying the frame-owner-change requirement rather than cutting at every formula onset.
items.evidence: Jer.25.31 closes with the bare neum-YHWH formula and Jer.25.32 opens with the koh-amar-tsevaot formula, both byte-confirmed as the same divine voice with no embedded or quoted second speaker in view anywhere in this span. Jer.25.33's description of the slain introduces no fresh addressee or formula that would argue for a further cut. The discourse-imperative opening at Jer.25.30, “Therefore prophesy against them all these words” (web:Jer.25.30), is a genuine tier-1 seam distinguishing this unit from the cup complex before it. judgment_oracle fits the roaring-lion and courtroom-controversy content well.
tier_citations: byte tier: oshb:Jer.25.30, oshb:Jer.25.31 (neum closure), oshb:Jer.25.32 (koh-amar tsevaot onset)

items.claim: The row's vocative shift at 25:34 is a genuine addressee-shift seam distinguishing the shepherds' direct address from the third-person description just before it, and the row honestly discloses the lion-image inclusio bracketing 25:30 and 25:38 as a real rival for reading the whole as one continuous poem, reducing its own confidence accordingly.
items.evidence: “Wail, you shepherds, and cry” (web:Jer.25.34) is a byte-confirmed direct second-person vocative, a genuine shift from 25:33's third-person register describing the unburied slain. The row itself names the echo between “against his fold” (web:Jer.25.30) and “left his covert, as the lion” (web:Jer.25.38) as an argument for reading that whole span as one sustained piece, and holds its own boundary at reduced confidence with a frontier flag on that account rather than concealing the tension.

items.claim: The row establishes a sound warrant for its opening edge at 26:1 but states no warrant at all for its closing edge at 26:6, never citing or discussing the participant and scene shift that opens immediately after at 26:7.
items.evidence: The row's boundary rationale and its full evidence list both stop at Jer.26.6 and never mention Jer.26.7, where a new set of participants enters -- “The priests and the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in Yahweh’s house” (web:Jer.26.7) -- and the narrative turns from Yahweh's private instruction to Jeremiah into public reaction, continuing into a seizure and a death-sentence demand at Jer.26.8-9. That scene shift is real and would itself support a tier-1 boundary at the 26:6/26:7 seam, but the row supplies no warrant for stopping there rather than continuing past it -- its cited evidence carries the opening boundary but not the closing one.
tier_citations: byte tier: oshb:Jer.26.6, oshb:Jer.26.7 (scene shift unaddressed by the row)
